page: Microsoft Azure D16als_v6 is a virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V, driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 32.0 GB, yielding a 2.0 GB per-core memory ratio. The server configuration includes no local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, utilizing remote storage volumes for persistent data operations.

Hardware capabilities include advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptography flags. In benchmark evaluations, the processor exhibits top-quartile single-core compute performance, recording 3,080.17 in stress-ng and 2,103.0 in Geekbench single-core testing. Multi-core performance aligns with median cloud benchmarks, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,569.0, a PassMark CPU score of 26,237.74, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 104.52 GB/sec.

Memory throughput exhibits distinct behavioral tiers: while small-block cached read operations reach 1,216.64 GB/sec, large uncached read bandwidth drops to 36.85 GB/sec, placing it in the lower performance quartile for uncached memory access. The reduced RAM ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for execution pipelines that do not demand expansive memory footprints. The profile suits code compilation pipelines, web application serving, text-processing services, and mid-tier API endpoints.
description: Microsoft Azure D16als_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 16 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Configured with a 2.0 GB per-core ratio, it allocates 8 physical cores via hyperthreading without bundled local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Compute evaluations show strong top-quartile single-core execution alongside median multi-core output across Geekbench and PassMark suites. Vector math and cryptography are accelerated via AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The architecture experiences lower uncached memory read bandwidth, yet small cached reads and text processing benchmarks remain competitive. By minimizing memory footprint and relying entirely on remote storage, the instance presents an efficient footprint for compute-centric application tiers, CI/CD compilation, and distributed microservices.
